setup: A non-production account under accounts/<domain>/ with profile.json (admin key), no git repo in that folder, and lifecycle hooks enabled on the account for Contact only. For eval 3, a deployed script <prefix>-dev whose index.js starts an async IIFE and ends with a console.log line. For eval 4, a deployed script <prefix>-dev that was run once by scriptCode, then fixed and redeployed. Replace <domain> and <prefix> in the prompts.

evals.prompt: Create a script on <domain> that I can run on demand and that returns how many contacts the account has.
evals.expected_output: Lays out accounts/<domain>/scripts/<prefix>/ by hand from assets/index.js, asks for an API key for the variables, deploys to dev without prompts, checks status, and runs it by _id after a yes.
expectations: Does not run ./prolibu script create, sync or test, and never --watch in the foreground
index.js requires the repo's lib with ../../../../lib/… and ends with the main() call that awaits Events.init()
Asks the user for the API key and puts it in config.json variables, not in the code
Deploys with ./prolibu script dev --domain <domain> --prefix <prefix> --no-git after a yes, and reads the output for 'Failed to PATCH'
Runs scripts/script.js status and then scripts/script.js run … --confirmed, and reports the count from output

evals.prompt: Hazme un script que, cada vez que se actualice un contacto en <domain>, guarde el nombre en mayúsculas.
evals.expected_output: Answers in Spanish. Checks that Contact is enabled for lifecycle hooks, writes a Contact.beforeUpdate handler that changes eventData.doc, warns that it fires on real records and about the dev and production copies, and deploys only after a yes.
expectations: Answers in Spanish
Reads GET /v2/preference/read and confirms Contact is in integrations.lifecycleHooks.enabledEntities before writing anything
Puts "Contact" in config.json lifecycleHooks and uses Events.on('Contact.beforeUpdate', …) changing eventData.doc, not eventData.payload
Says the hook runs on real contacts as soon as it is deployed, and that only one copy should keep it
Changes the name only when it is not already uppercase, or otherwise explains how it avoids re-triggering itself

evals.prompt: My script <prefix>-dev on <domain> returns output null and no error. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Reads the entry, sees the async work is not the last statement, explains the run ends when the last statement's promise settles, fixes it, redeploys and runs again.
expectations: Explains that work not awaited by the last statement is cut off without an error
Moves the async call so it is the last statement (or awaits it from main) and keeps output assigned
Redeploys with the CLI, checks status, and runs with scripts/script.js run after a yes

evals.prompt: I deployed a fix to <prefix>-dev on <domain>, but GET /v2/script/run?scriptId=<prefix>-dev still shows the old error.
evals.expected_output: Explains that a run by scriptCode serves cached old code, checks with status that the new code is on the account, and runs by _id.
expectations: Says a run by scriptCode can execute code cached before the deploy, and that _id avoids it
Runs scripts/script.js status and confirms code.matchesBundle is true
Runs with scripts/script.js run (by _id), not with the scriptCode URL

evals.prompt: Schedule <prefix> on <domain> to run every weekday at 7 am Bogotá time.
evals.expected_output: Sets scheduledTask with periodicity and timeZone through the API helper on one copy's _id after a yes, notes that deploys keep it, and reads it back.
expectations: Uses PATCH /v2/script/<_id> with scheduledTask {periodicity: '0 7 * * 1-5', timeZone: 'America/Bogota'} and --confirmed only after a yes
Does not try to put the schedule in config.json
Schedules only one copy and says the other must not carry the same trigger
Reads it back with scripts/script.js status (scheduledTask) and mentions GET /v2/script/schedulerStatus for checking the registration
